items.title: FineGrainedFP8: modules_to_not_convert never matches on text-only loads of multimodal checkpoints (silent quality corruption)
items.body:
**Summary.** `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` ships `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert`
with multimodal-wrapper paths (`model.language_model.layers...`). When the checkpoint is
loaded through `AutoModelForCausalLM` the text stack is named `model.layers...`, so none of
the exclusion patterns match. The FineGrainedFP8 quantizer then converts modules the vendor
intended to keep in bf16 (e.g. the PLE projections `ple.key_proj` / `ple.value_proj`,
hyper-connection mixers, linear-attention conv/in_proj):
their bf16 checkpoint weights are silently cast to fp8 **without any scale**, corrupting the
values. Nothing fails at load; quality is just degraded (and in our case a downstream dtype
mismatch happened to surface it).

**Repro.** load FP8 repo with AutoModelForCausalLM, inspect
`model.model.layers[1].ple.key_proj` → converted/`fp8` despite checkpoint tensor being BF16
and the module being listed (with wrapper prefix) in modules_to_not_convert.

**Suggested fix.** Prefix-normalize modules_to_not_convert against the instantiated model
(same logic that already remaps checkpoint keys between wrapper and text-only layouts), or
match on suffix segments. Workaround we used: rewrite the list at load time
(`m.replace("model.language_model.", "model.")`) and pass a fresh FineGrainedFP8Config.

---
Found during day-0 bring-up of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` on transformers main (5.16.0.dev0); all three verified with local patches, model loads and generates correctly with fixes applied. Cross-report on the model repo: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8/discussions/2
We also have working CPU-offload bounces for the CUDA-only fp8 paths (grouped experts + FP8Linear) that made the 176B-total checkpoint run on a single 96GB GPU + 128GB RAM - happy to open a PR if there is interest.

items.title: Chunk conversion op silently produces unequal chunks when the fused tensor is not divisible by the target count
items.body:
### System Info

- transformers 5.16.0.dev0 (current main)
- python 3.12.6, Windows 11 (not platform specific)

### Reproduction

The v5 dynamic loading API's `Chunk` op (`src/transformers/core_model_loading.py`, class `Chunk`) splits a fused tensor for targets like q/k/v. Its guard only compares chunk COUNT against the target count:

```python
chunks = tuple(chunk.contiguous() for chunk in torch.chunk(tensor, sizes, dim=self.dim))
if len(input_dict) > 1 or len(target_patterns) == 1 or len(chunks) != len(target_patterns):
    raise ValueError(f"Failed to convert {kwargs.get('full_layer_name')}")
```

`torch.chunk` returns unequal chunks when the tensor size is not divisible by the requested count, and can still return exactly as many chunks as there are targets. Then every downstream consumer receives differently sized tensors:

```python
import torch
from transformers.core_model_loading import Chunk

op = Chunk(dim=0)
t = {"x": [torch.arange(5.)]}
out = op.convert(t, source_patterns=["x"], target_patterns=["a", "b"], full_layer_name="demo.layer")
print({k: tuple(v.shape) for k, v in out.items()})
```

Output on current main - no error, wrong shapes:

```text
{'a': (3,), 'b': (2,)}
```

In a real `from_pretrained` conversion this surfaces either as a confusing per-target shape mismatch error far from the cause, or worse: silently re-initializing weights under `ignore_mismatched_sizes`, which corrupts the model without any signal.

### Expected behavior

Since the op's own contract is "Split a tensor along dim into equally sized chunks", an indivisible split should fail loudly at the conversion site with a clear message naming the violated contract and the layer, instead of producing silently unequal chunks. Every registered `Chunk` usage in the codebase splits equal-sized siblings by construction, so a divisibility check would not reject any legitimate existing use.

Duplicate check: searched open/closed issues and PRs around torch.chunk uneven splits, Chunk.convert, and ignore_mismatched_sizes silent re-init; nothing tracks this.

items.title: StopStringCriteria raises a bare 'substring not found' when the tokenizer vocab cannot round-trip its validation probe
items.body:
### System Info

- transformers 5.16.0.dev0 (current main)
- python 3.12.6, Windows 11 (not platform specific)

### Reproduction

`StopStringCriteria` validates stop strings against a tokenizer vocabulary by re-decoding a fixed ASCII probe prefix plus each vocab token and stripping the prefix back off (`_clean_tokenizer_vocab` in `src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py`). When a tokenizer's tokens cannot survive that decode round trip, `str.index` raises a bare:

```text
ValueError: substring not found
```

instead of anything a user can act on. Minimal repro with a word-level vocab over a non-latin script:

```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import WordLevel
from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Whitespace

from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
from transformers.generation.stopping_criteria import StopStringCriteria

vocab = {"你": 0, "好": 1, "<unk>": 2}
backend_tokenizer = Tokenizer(WordLevel(vocab=vocab, unk_token="<unk>"))
backend_tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = Whitespace()
tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_object=backend_tokenizer, unk_token="<unk>")

criteria = StopStringCriteria(tokenizer=tokenizer, stop_strings=["你好"])
```

Current output:

```text
  File ".../stopping_criteria.py", line 373, in clean_tokenizer_vocab
    token_string = token_string[token_string.index(static_prefix) + len(static_prefix) :]
ValueError: substring not found
```

Affected vocabularies are not exotic: any word-level vocab whose entries do not round trip the ASCII probe - non-latin-script word-level vocabs, and even all-ASCII word-level vocabs that simply lack the probe letters.

### Expected behavior

The module already has a designed diagnostic for exactly this situation (a ValueError mentioning that stop strings cannot be matched against a vocabulary containing unusual characters), but the round-trip failure path never reaches it because the exception surfaces from `str.index` first. The constructor should catch the lookup failure in `_clean_tokenizer_vocab` and raise the intended diagnostic instead of leaking the raw `substring not found`.

Related but different: #46519 (CJK byte-fragment matching inside StopStringCriteria, since fixed) and #35244 (vocab_size vs len(tokenizer) index errors).

items.title: Continuous batching is loud by default: WARNING logs and progress bars on a plain generate_batch
items.body:
A plain `generate_batch` call at default verbosity prints a stream of warnings and a progress bar; `model.generate()` prints nothing. Users embedding CB in a serving loop or trainer get this on every manager start.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, GenerationConfig

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0")

prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": "Hi!"}], add_generation_prompt=True)["input_ids"]
model.generate_batch([prompt] * 4, generation_config=GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=16))
```

## Outcome

```
Solving 4 requests:   0%|          | 0/4 [00:00<?, ?request/s]
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - `eos_token_id` not set in GenerationConfig. Setting to -1 (disabled).
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - Continuous batching is much better when using flash attention. Switching from sdpa to flash_attention_3. If you need to use eager or sdpa, use paged|eager or paged|sdpa as the `attn_implementation`.
[transformers] You do not have `flash_attn` installed, using `paged|kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` from the `kernels` library instead!
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - Warming up for continuous batching...
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - Warming up completed in 8.39s.
Solving 4 requests: 100%|██████████| 4/4 [00:10<00:00,  2.56s/request]
```

(On TP runs there is additionally `Setting NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT = 0 ...` per rank, and each subsequent manager in the same process repeats the attention-switch and warmup messages.)

Most of these are informational (attention implementation switched, warmup started/finished, NCCL env tweak) and none of them describes a problem with the user's call; at default verbosity they belong at `info`/`debug`. The progress bar should follow the same convention as the rest of the library (opt-in or tied to logging verbosity), since `generate_batch` is used programmatically inside trainers and servers.

## Expected behavior

Silence at default verbosity, matching `model.generate()`. Keep genuinely actionable warnings (e.g. `eos_token_id` unset) at `warning`; move status messages to `info`; gate the `Solving n requests` tqdm behind an argument or the logging level.

## System info

transformers main (a353632), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.12, NVIDIA H100 80GB.

items.title: Continuous batching CUDA-graph capture crashes under distributed runs (allocator internal assert)
items.body:
Found while benchmarking continuous batching throughput on Qwen3-30B-A3B with tp_size=4; later also hit on a 2-process data-parallel run with dense Qwen3-0.6B, so the trigger is distributed + graph capture, not the model type.

## Reproduction

A sustained sampled workload (1024 prompts x 256 new tokens, `max_memory_percent=0.8`, tp_size=4) reproduces within ~5 minutes; a handful of short greedy requests does NOT trigger it, so the workload shape matters. Run with `torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py`:

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Run: torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py
# (4x H100 80GB; crashes during graph capture within ~2 min of the workload starting)

import os
import time

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, GenerationConfig
from transformers.distributed.configuration_utils import DistributedConfig
from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import ContinuousBatchingConfig

MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507"
NUM_PROMPTS = 1024
MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 256


def main():
    rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        MODEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size=int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])),
    )
    prompts = []
    for i in range(NUM_PROMPTS):
        content = f"Explain topic number {i} in a few sentences." + " Give plenty of detail." * (i % 4)
        prompts.append(
            tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
                [{"role": "user", "content": content}], add_generation_prompt=True
            )["input_ids"]
        )
    manager = model.init_continuous_batching(
        generation_config=GenerationConfig(
            max_new_tokens=MAX_NEW_TOKENS, do_sample=True, temperature=1.0,
            eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        ),
        continuous_batching_config=ContinuousBatchingConfig(max_memory_percent=0.8),
    )
    manager.start()
    cpu_group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")

    request_ids = manager.add_requests(prompts, max_new_tokens=MAX_NEW_TOKENS) or []
    got = 0
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    while got < len(request_ids):
        out = manager.get_result(timeout=600)  # the background thread dies with the assert (in the logs);
        # get_result then never returns a result (#48301 makes this raise instead)
        if out is None:
            raise TimeoutError(f"{got}/{len(request_ids)}")
        got += 1
    if rank == 0:
        print(f"completed {got} requests in {time.perf_counter() - t0:.1f}s (no crash)")
    dist.barrier(group=cpu_group)
    manager.stop(block=True, timeout=120)
    os._exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Outcome

The background thread dies during CUDA graph capture:

items.title: Native TP does not shard qwen3_vl_moe experts (weights fully replicated per rank)
items.body:
Found while testing native TP on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B; the sibling arch qwen3_5_moe shards correctly with the same code, which makes the comparison easy. Related but distinct from #48204: that draft adds an expert-parallel path; this issue is about the plain tp_size-only path silently replicating the experts.

## Reproduction

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText
from transformers.distributed.configuration_utils import DistributedConfig

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct", dtype=torch.bfloat16, distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size=4)
)
print(torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 1e9)  # expected ~15 GB/rank, observed 60.3 GB/rank
```

## Outcome

The model loads without error but each rank holds 60.3 GB: the full 30B-A3B weights. Expert weights are not sharded (for comparison, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`, arch `qwen3_5_moe`, shards to
10.5 GB/rank with the same code). Consequences observed:

- any training attempt OOMs immediately (weights + grads alone exceed 80 GB)
- continuous batching on the TP model crashes in the paged cache with `index_copy_(): Destination slice shape: 4 128 ... source slice shape: 1 128`: the cache is sized for the config's 4 KV heads while the attention layers are sharded to 1 KV head per rank, so the two disagree (attention appears sharded while the MoE is not).

Root cause: `Qwen3VLMoeTextConfig.base_model_tp_plan` carries dense-style `layers.*.mlp.gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj` entries, paths that do not exist in the MoE layers (experts live at `layers.*.mlp.experts.*`), so no pattern matches the expert weights and they replicate. The sibling `qwen3_5_moe` plan has the fused-expert entries (`experts.gate_up_proj: packed_colwise`, `experts.down_proj: rowwise`, `experts: moe_tp_experts`), which is why it shards correctly.

Precedent: the sibling arch had the identical bug, reported in #45125 and fixed by #45124 (add `_tp_plan` to the ForConditionalGeneration wrapper). That fix was never mirrored to qwen3_vl_moe, which is exactly why the comparison above splits the way it does. #41570 (uneven memory on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B multi-GPU) may be an earlier symptom sighting.

## Expected behavior

Either a complete TP plan for `qwen3_vl_moe` (experts sharded like the other MoE archs), or a load-time error when parts of the model have no TP mapping, instead of silent replication.

## System info

items.title: Native TP has no KV-head replication: tp_size > num_key_value_heads fails mid-forward
items.body:
Found while testing native TP on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (4 KV heads).

## Reproduction

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 repro.py
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.distributed.configuration_utils import DistributedConfig

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct"  # num_key_value_heads=4, head_dim=128
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size=8)
)
batch = tokenizer(["Some text " * 100], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
model(**batch)
```

## Outcome

Loading and sharding succeed, the forward fails in attention:

```
  key_states = self.k_norm(self.k_proj(hidden_states).view(hidden_shape)).transpose(1, 2)
RuntimeError: shape '[4, 178, -1, 128]' is invalid for input of size 45568
```

With 4 KV heads and head_dim 128, k_proj has 512 output features; colwise TP8 leaves 64 per rank, less than one head, and the `(..., -1, head_dim)` view fails. Nothing warned at load time.

The same model with `tp_size=4` (1 KV head per rank) works.

Possibly an earlier sighting of the same class: #40953 (gpt-oss-120b, 8 KV heads, failing at tp_plan="auto" on 16 GPUs; closed without this diagnosis).

## Expected behavior

Replicate KV heads across TP ranks when `tp_size > num_key_value_heads` (what vLLM does), or at minimum raise a clear error at load time ("tp_size=8 exceeds num_key_value_heads=4") instead of a reshape error mid-forward.

items.title: Native TP breaks on Qwen3.5/3.6 hybrids: reshape error in linear-attention layers
items.body:
Found while testing native TP training on recent Qwen models.

## Reproduction

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 repro.py
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.distributed.configuration_utils import DistributedConfig

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size=8)
)
batch = tokenizer(["Some text " * 100], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
model(**batch)
```

## Outcome

Model loads and shards (10.5 GB/rank for 35B-A3B, consistent with TP8), but the forward fails:

```
RuntimeError: shape '[4, 178, -1, 256]' is invalid for input of size 45568
```

The reshape uses the full-attention `head_dim` (256) on the output of a projection that the TP plan sharded, in a linear-attention layer whose projections have their own head dims (`linear_key_head_dim`, `linear_value_head_dim`). The auto TP plan appears not to cover the linear-attention (gated delta) layers of the qwen3_5/qwen3_6 architecture correctly.

Not investigated further; non-hybrid MoE shards and runs fine with the same code. Secondary observation on the same path: `torch.optim.AdamW` defaults fail on a TP model with `aten._foreach_mul_.Scalar got mixed torch.Tensor and DTensor` (some params are not DTensors); `foreach=False` works around it (#48204 already handles this class of problem on the Trainer side with per-parameter AdamW).

items.title: Continuous batching does not support hybrid linear-attention models (all Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8)
items.body:
Follow-up to #48298: with that fixed, the next wall for recent Qwen models is architectural.

## Reproduction

(Requires the composite-config fix from #48299 first; without it the same call dies earlier on `num_key_value_heads ... not found in the config`.)

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoTokenizer, GenerationConfig

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0")

prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": "Hi!"}], add_generation_prompt=True)["input_ids"]
outputs = model.generate_batch([prompt], generation_config=GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=16))
```

## Outcome

The background generation thread dies in `PagedAttentionCache.__init__`:

```
ValueError: Invalid group type: linear_attention
```

Qwen3.5-style models interleave linear-attention layers with full attention (`full_attention_interval: 4`, i.e. 3 out of 4 layers are linear attention). The paged cache only implements `full_attention` and `sliding_attention` allocators; linear-attention layers need a per-request recurrent state (fixed size, no paging) instead of a KV block pool.

Every recent Qwen release (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8) is such a hybrid, so continuous batching (and therefore `transformers serve`) supports none of them. Regular `generate()` works.

For scale: standard training forwards on these models work fine (verified: SFT on Qwen3.5-2B converges normally with sdpa), only the CB path is blocked.

## Expected behavior

Either support linear-attention state in the CB cache (a `LinearAttentionCacheAllocator` holding a fixed-size recurrent state per request, analogous to what vLLM does for hybrid Qwen3.5), or fail at `init_continuous_batching` time with a clear "model architecture not supported by continuous batching" error instead of a background-thread crash that surfaces as a silent timeout (see also the fail-fast problem, #48298, fixed by #48301).

This one is a feature request rather than a bug fix; not attempted yet.

items.title: Async continuous batching crashes at start() if no request is queued yet
items.body:
Found while benchmarking train-while-generating setups: whether `manager.start()` works depends on a race with the first `add_request`.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, GenerationConfig

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")

manager = model.init_continuous_batching(
    generation_config=GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=16, eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id)
)
manager.start()          # background thread bootstraps immediately...
import time; time.sleep(2)
manager.add_request(tokenizer("Hi")["input_ids"])  # ...before any request exists
```

Needs the async batching path active (flash attention available, CUDA graphs on: the default on H100). With sdpa/eager (async off) the same sequence works.

## Outcome

```
ERROR - Error in generation loop: Failed to bootstrap the first batch.
RuntimeError: Failed to bootstrap the first batch.
```

In `_run_generation_loop`, the async path bootstraps the first batch unconditionally at thread start and raises when `prepare_next_batch()` finds an empty queue. The main loop right below it handles the empty-queue case fine (waits on `_has_new_requests`). So a manager started before the first request dies, one started after works: user code that does `manager.start()` then submits from another thread wins or loses this race nondeterministically. Combined with the silent-timeout problem (#48298, fixed by #48301), the visible symptom is requests that never return.

## Expected behavior

The bootstrap should wait for the first request (same as the main loop) instead of raising.
Fix proposed in #XXXX; with it, start() followed by a late add_request generates normally.

## System info

items.title: Continuous batching crashes on every VLM: config attributes read from the top-level config
items.body:
Found while running text-only continuous batching on VLMs. All recent Qwen releases are ForConditionalGeneration composites, so today this blocks CB (and `transformers serve` continuous batching) for all of them.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoTokenizer, GenerationConfig

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct"  # any ForConditionalGeneration model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0")

prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": "Hi!"}], add_generation_prompt=True)["input_ids"]
outputs = model.generate_batch([prompt], generation_config=GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=16))
```

## Outcome

The background generation thread dies immediately:

```
ValueError: num_key_value_heads or num_attention_heads could not be found in the config:
Qwen3_5Config { ... "text_config": { "num_key_value_heads": 8, ... } ... }
```

`PagedAttentionCache` and `resolve_continuous_batching_config` read decoder attributes (`num_key_value_heads`, `num_hidden_layers`, `head_dim`, `sliding_window`, ...) from the config they are given, and the manager passes `self.model.config`: the top-level composite config, which keeps those attributes on `text_config`.

Text-only generation through VLMs is a fully supported `generate()` path, and all recent Qwen releases (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8) are `ForConditionalGeneration` composites, so this blocks continuous batching (and `transformers serve` continuous batching) for all of them.

Secondary UX problem, hit while debugging this: after the background thread dies, `manager.add_requests` keeps accepting requests and `get_result` returns `None` forever. The `fatal_error` attribute is set but nothing surfaces it to a caller that isn't polling it: a plain `generate_batch` user just times out with no error.

## Fix

Resolve against `config.get_text_config()` at the three call sites in `ContinuousBatchingManager` (`resolve_continuous_batching_config`, `PagedAttentionCache`, `ContinuousBatchProcessor`). `get_text_config()` returns `self` for text-only configs, so this is a no-op for the existing paths.

Implemented on branch, with the fix, Qwen3.5-2B gets past config resolution (it then hits the separate hybrid linear-attention limitation, issue TODO); end-to-end validation runs on a non-hybrid VLM (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct).

items.title: `paged|sdpa` silently computes non-causal attention on a standard forward
items.body:
Found while testing training and continuous batching on one weight copy (training forward on the same model a CB manager generates with). Filing separately because the failure is silent and can bite anyone who runs a regular forward on a model with an attached CB manager.

### What happens

`ContinuousBatchingManager.switch_to_cb_friendly_attn` switches the whole model to a paged attention implementation. A standard forward in that state goes through `sdpa_attention_paged_forward`, which treats `cache` as optional (`kwargs.pop("cache", None)`) and runs plain SDPA when it is absent. But in paged mode the model builds no causal mask, so `attn_mask` is `None` and `is_causal` is never set: the forward is fully bidirectional. No error, no warning. (`paged|flash_attention_*` at least raises a `TypeError`, since `cache` is a
required positional there; `paged|eager` has the same silent problem as sdpa.)

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model_id = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0", attn_implementation="sdpa"
)

batch = tokenizer(["The capital of France is Paris."], return_tensors="pt").to("cuda:0")
labels = batch["input_ids"].clone()

with torch.no_grad():
    ref_loss = model(**batch, labels=labels).loss.item()

model.set_attn_implementation("paged|sdpa")  # what the CB manager does to the model
with torch.no_grad():
    paged_loss = model(**batch, labels=labels).loss.item()  # expected: raise. actual: silent wrong result

print(f"sdpa loss:       {ref_loss:.4f}")
print(f"paged|sdpa loss: {paged_loss:.4f}")
assert abs(ref_loss - paged_loss) < 0.1, (
    "paged|sdpa silently computed different (non-causal) attention on a standard forward"
)
```

```
sdpa loss:       3.0899
paged|sdpa loss: 1.9871
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/fsx/qgallouedec/cb_train/issues/01-paged-sdpa-silent-noncausal/repro.py", line 33, in <module>
    assert abs(ref_loss - paged_loss) < 0.1, (
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError: paged|sdpa silently computed different (non-causal) attention on a standard forward
```

Measured (Qwen3-0.6B, bf16, H100, padded 2-sequence batch): loss 2.8371 vs 4.0290 for sdpa, max logit diff 22.5, and backward "works" (grad_norm 936 vs 199 for the correct forward).

### Expected behavior

Either
- raise when a paged implementation is invoked without CB kwargs, or 
- fall back to the true non-paged implementation.

The fallback is the more useful behavior: it makes a model with an attached CB manager directly usable for training forwards on the same weights, verified: with the fallback, rollouts of a live CB manager pick up concurrent training within seconds.

Fix proposed in #XXXX (coming): paged forwards delegate to their base implementation when `cache` is
absent, and mask creation resolves 2D-or-absent masks through the base implementation's mask
function. After it, `paged|sdpa` == `sdpa` and `paged|eager` == `eager` exactly (logit diff
0.0)

Repro script and numbers: `repro.py` in this folder. transformers main (a353632), torch 2.13.0+cu130, H100.
